title: Curt Cignetti defends Indiana’s resume, says Hoosiers ‘ripped the heart out of’ Ohio State
content:
Indiana coach Curt Cignetti said the Hoosiers “ripped the heart out of” Ohio State when he went on the offensive to combat doubts about his program’s resume on Monday. It was the latest in a string of comments from Cignetti, who has been critical of the College Football Playoff selection committee and others who have questioned the Hoosiers’ credibility on the field.

Last Tuesday, Cignetti watched Indiana (9-1, 6-1 Big Ten) fall from fourth to ninth in the weekly CFP rankings even though the Hoosiers did not play the Saturday prior. Afterward, he tweeted: “Bad losses don’t count anymore? Are first downs still 10 yards?”

A week before that, he went on the radio and said the “SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN. … And that’s why you see all these SEC teams up there and some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten not quite as high.”

Cignetti’s Ohio State comment came in the middle of an extended defense of the Hoosiers’ schedule.

“Well, you know, we don’t play anybody,” Cignetti told reporters Monday. “We have a soft schedule, right? That’s all I’ve heard around here for three years because people love to discredit us and what we’ve accomplished.”

Indiana just bolstered its resume with a top-25 win against a USC squad that was ranked 19th in last week’s CFP rankings. The Hoosiers’ lone loss came to Ohio State when the Buckeyes still had a healthy Julian Sayin at quarterback. Indiana knocked Sayin out of that game with a shoulder injury, and the 2025 Heisman Trophy finalist hasn’t played since. Ohio State has gone 1-2 in the three games without Sayin and has fallen to 7-3 (5-2) this season. Indiana lost that game when receiver Nick Marsh failed to get his foot inbounds for what should have been the game-winning touchdown reception. That was the Hoosiers’ only loss in the past 26 games.

“You saw what happened. We knocked the quarterback out,” Cignetti said. “We ripped the heart out of that team. They haven’t been the same since without the quarterback. But all I hear about is how we lost to a three-loss team. That was a team picked to win a national championship that led Texas 95 percent of the game at Texas. We missed a layup. You know what? They won; we didn’t. But we missed a layup. You know, that’s why we’re not 26-0, we’re 25-1.”

Cignetti went up and down much of Indiana’s Big Ten slate so far. He mentioned how Northwestern was a good team that played a tough game and reached the top 25 shortly after but has lost a couple of games since an injury to starting quarterback Aidan Chiles. That win has lost some value as the Wildcats have fallen to 6-4 (3-4), but Alabama has received some credit from the rankings committee for beating Mississippi State when it had quarterback Kamario Taylor in the lineup. The Bulldogs are 4-6.

“You get tired of the narrative sometimes, you know?” Cignetti said. “Quality win because Joe Smith was playing at the time. They ain’t won a game since, but it was a quality win back then.”

He pointed out that Nebraska was 5-0 (now 6-4, 3-4) when Indiana visited Lincoln for a game and overcame an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to escape with a 20-17 triumph.

“They had a hard time rebounding from that, OK? Wasn’t a pretty win in a lot of people’s eyes, but from a coach’s standpoint, showed a lot of competitive character to me and people that know football,” Cignetti said.

A week after the Ohio State game, Indiana traveled to Michigan (5-5, 2-5) and won an ugly, defensive battle against the Wolverines in overtime, 13-6, with a hampered quarterback in Josh Hoover.

“That’s an easy one right up in Ann Arbor: 4-2 Michigan, 112,000 (fans), you know, with a quarterback that’s not 100 percent,” Cignetti said.

Cignetti pointed out that Minnesota (5-5, 3-4) was 5-2 entering their game — a 23-16 overtime win for the Hoosiers — and how USC was 7-2 entering this past Saturday’s contest.

We’ll see how the committee treats Indiana on Tuesday night. There aren’t many opportunities left in the regular season for the Hoosiers to add quality wins. They play at Washington this weekend. The Huskies are 6-4 (3-4) and have been mediocre to average this season. Indiana closes out the regular season with its rivalry game against Purdue, which is 3-7 (2-5). The Hoosiers will be considerable favorites in both games and seem prime for another trip to the Big Ten title game.

“But, look, it’s all going to play out on the field,” Cignetti said. “You know, good for entertainment. I’m sure this will get a lot of nice hits and play, but our guys understand that it’ll play out on the field. The good thing about it is I think it feeds into our motivation and our chip. That’s why I’m not afraid to keep it alive. And you know what? I’m 65 years old, and I really don’t give a s—.”
